title: Unit 4 Mixed Review Core Test
description: Practice and explain unit 4 mixed review.

questions.questionText: Solve 3x + 5 = 11.
questions.explanation: Subtract 5 from both sides, then divide 6 by 3.

questions.questionText: Which expression is equivalent to 2(x + 2) + x?
questions.explanation: Distribute 2 to both terms, then combine 2x and x.

questions.questionText: Check (2, 4) in y = x + 2 and x + y = 6. Which statement is true?
questions.correctAnswer: The pair satisfies both equations.
questions.explanation: The first gives 4; the sum in the second is 6. Both checks work.
options: The pair satisfies only the first equation.
The pair satisfies only the second equation.

questions.questionText: The equation 2x + 2 = 2x + 3 has how many solutions?
questions.correctAnswer: No solutions
questions.explanation: Subtracting 2x gives 2 = 3, a false statement.

questions.questionText: What does the intersection (2, 4) of two line graphs represent?
questions.correctAnswer: An ordered pair satisfying both equations
questions.explanation: At the intersection the same x and y coordinates lie on both lines simultaneously.
options: Only the slope of the first line
Only the intercept of the second line
An ordered pair satisfying both equations

questions.questionText: A student expands -2(x - 2) as -2x - 4, then solves -2(x - 2) = 6. Which correction and solution are right?
questions.correctAnswer: The constant should be +4; x = -1.
questions.explanation: The product of two negatives is positive. Then -2x + 4 = 6 gives x = -1.
options: Only the x sign should change; x = 5.

questions.questionText: For which k does 3(x + 2) = 3x + k have infinitely many solutions, and what happens if k is one greater?
questions.correctAnswer: k = 6; one greater gives no solution.
questions.explanation: Expansion gives 3x + 6 = 3x + k. Equal constants give an identity; unequal constants give a contradiction.
options: k = 2; one greater gives one solution.
k = 6; one greater gives one solution.
k = 6; one greater gives no solution.
k = 7; one greater gives infinitely many solutions.

questions.questionText: Solve 2x + 3y = 20 and 3x - 2y = 4. Verify your pair in both equations.
questions.explanation: Multiply the equations by 2 and 3 and add: 13x = 52. Then x = 4 and y = 4; both original totals match.

questions.questionText: Two taxi fares are A = 6 + 2d and B = 5d. A learner says equality occurs at d = 6. What is the correct distance and a check?
questions.correctAnswer: d = 2; both fares are $10.
questions.explanation: Set 6 + 2d = 5d, so 3d = 6. Substitution gives equal fares at d = 2.

questions.questionText: A system is x + y = 11, 2x + 2y = 24. A learner divides the second equation by 2 and claims infinitely many solutions. What was missed?
questions.correctAnswer: Its right side becomes 12, contradicting x + y = 11.
questions.explanation: Matching variable coefficients are not enough. The right sides must match too; these equations give distinct parallel lines.
options: The equations actually have exactly one solution.
Its right side becomes 12, contradicting x + y = 11.
Dividing an equation by 2 is never allowed.
Only the origin solves the system.
